_comment: Copy this to ~/.config/hestia-antideadzone/config.json and edit. JSON has no comments, so any '_xxx_help' key is documentation only and is ignored by the daemon.
_device_name_match_help: Case-insensitive substring to pick your pad if you have multiple input devices (e.g. 'Xbox', 'DualSense', '8BitDo'). Leave empty to auto-pick the first thing that looks like a gamepad. Run list-devices.py to see exact names.
_profile_help: Each of 'left'/'right' carries its own settings, including deadzone_shape, so the two sticks can use different shapes (e.g. axial on the right stick for a game with its own per-axis deadzone, radial on the left for smooth movement). deadzone: 0-1, fraction of stick travel ignored near center (raise if you have stick drift). anti_deadzone: 0-1, the output floor the instant the stick leaves the deadzone -- this is the setting that defeats a game's own internal deadzone, same concept as Steam Input's. curve: 1.0 = linear; >1.0 gives more fine control near center at the cost of feeling 'slower' to ramp up (try 1.5-2.0); <1.0 is the opposite (twitchier near center). deadzone_shape (per stick, one of three): 'radial' (recommended default -- circular, diagonals stay smooth and proportional at every deflection); 'axial' (true per-axis deadzone/anti-deadzone with a FLAT per-axis threshold, matching games whose own deadzone is also axial, e.g. many UE4/5 titles like Hogwarts Legacy -- reliably restores movement on a diagonal push the game would otherwise eat, but distorts angle noticeably near the deadzone edge, e.g. a shallow-angle push can snap toward 45 degrees, and needs more total deflection at an angle than straight on before anything registers); 'sloped_axial' (based on the published 'sloped scaled axial' deadzone -- each axis's own deadzone shrinks toward 0 as the OTHER axis approaches 0, so a near-cardinal push barely deadzones the off-axis at all, which removes the extra-push-at-an-angle threshold mismatch and meaningfully softens (but doesn't eliminate) the 45-degree snap; still floors each axis independently like axial, so it keeps axial's reliability against a downstream game's own per-axis deadzone -- recommended over plain axial for games with an axial deadzone unless you have a specific reason to want the flatter threshold).
_rescan_interval_help: Seconds between reconnect attempts while no matching controller is found. Each attempt just opens the /dev/input/event* nodes and reads capabilities -- a few ms of local syscalls -- so 1s or even lower isn't a meaningful CPU cost.
_reload_interval_help: Seconds between checks of this file's last-modified time. Lower = more responsive profile switches, higher = very slightly less overhead. 1 second is already fast enough to switch mid-game between menu screens.
_debug_sample_rate_help: Set to e.g. 30 to log every 30th stick event at DEBUG level for tuning. 0 disables.
